material.canon_label_hint: Projection-trust operational states: current, refreshing, stale, degraded, unavailable
exact_items: current: projection is up to date enough for normal read + write interaction
refreshing: slightly behind but actively catching up; read is fine, write may still be fine
stale: data is old enough that mutation-bearing actions should narrow or require refetch
degraded: projector or dependency failure means surface may be incomplete or partially wrong
unavailable: projection cannot currently support that surface; UI must fall back or disable
notes: New system concept: projection-trust must have exact operational states with specific action-gating implications; not just on/off

material.canon_label_hint: Action-gating split: read-only allows refreshing/stale/degraded, mutation requires current or revalidation
exact_items: low-risk read-only inspection: allowed on refreshing, often on stale, sometimes on degraded
precise navigation/deep-linking: usually allowed if target object identity valid
live mutation/approval/recovery/retry/cleanup: require current or direct canonical-runtime validation path
if surface is stale or degraded, GUI must not present mutation controls that imply hidden confidence
notes: New consumer obligation: action controls must gate on projection-trust state; stale/degraded surfaces must disable or narrow mutation controls

material.canon_label_hint: Canonical-validation rule: revalidate stale/degraded projection writes against authoritative runtime state

GUI should never guess that previously visible allowed_action_ids[] set is still valid if blocked projection is stale
notes: New runtime invariant: write from stale projection must trigger revalidation; allowed_action_ids[] freshness is not assumed
